artifact.version_note: 44-page published ICML 2026 paper. Title, ordered authors and proceedings footer read. Proceedings spells out two middle names omitted on the PDF. Matching arXiv v1 retained as Wrobel2024_arxiv.pdf.

contexts.evidence: Sections 3–5 present artifact suppression through effective operators and transformed-input averaging.
Section 3.2 and Appendix A.3 justify suppression, not universal removal, of transform-dependent artifacts.
contexts.proposed_replacement: Replace “removes the same grid artifact that DAVE targets” with “suppresses the same kind of grid artifact that DAVE targets”.

contexts.evidence: Appendix A.1.4 retains linear mean-centering; attention weights and normalization scale are conditioned.
contexts.proposed_replacement: Conservative propagation~\parencite{Ali2022AttnLRP} holds $A$ and the LayerNorm statistics fixed; DAVE~\parencite{Wrobel2024} also fixes $A$, but retains linear mean-centering while fixing the normalization scale. Both use the Value path through attention.

contexts.evidence: Sections 3.1–3.3 describe conditioned operators, patch-grid artifacts and spatial averaging; register mitigation is complementary.
Appendix A.1.2 and Algorithm 1 freeze attention and preserve the Value/output projections.
Appendix A.1.4 uses coupled linear centering, not the thesis pointwise map with frozen mean.
contexts.proposed_replacement: For our conditioned transport, both LayerNorm statistics are detached, making the layer pointwise affine; this differs from DAVE, which retains linear mean-centering while fixing the normalization scale~\parencite{Wrobel2024}.

contexts.evidence: Section 3.2 supports optional transform averaging to suppress grid artifacts; the numerical comparison is thesis evidence.
Section 3.1 and Appendix A.1.2 support the qualified resemblance to conditioned Value-only attribution.
DAVE already detaches attention; its LayerNorm mean-centering differs from the thesis convention (Appendix A.1).
contexts.proposed_replacement: We call this a conditioned forward pass inspired by DAVE~\parencite{Wrobel2024}, with the LayerNorm mean also frozen as specified below.

contexts.evidence: Appendix A.1.4, p. 15, and official make_centering_layer_norm retain centering; only inverse standard deviation is detached.
contexts.proposed_replacement: For our conditioned attribution, we compute $m,s$ from a detached copy $c=x.\mathrm{detach}()$, giving the pointwise affine map $x\mapsto w_{\mathrm{LN}}\odot(x-m(c))/s(c)+b_{\mathrm{LN}}$. This differs from DAVE~\parencite{Wrobel2024}, which retains linear mean-centering and freezes only the normalization scale.

contexts.evidence: The four rules adapt DAVE; they do not exactly reproduce its LayerNorm operator (Appendix A.1.4).
contexts.proposed_replacement: Replace “realize the detached-operator semantics of~\textcite{Wrobel2024}” with “implement conditioned attribution inspired by~\textcite{Wrobel2024}, with the LayerNorm mean additionally frozen,”.

contexts.evidence: Section 3.2 and Algorithm 2 support aligned averaging; thesis explicitly labels its different ranges/no-noise mode.
Sections 3.1–3.2 link patch-grid artifacts to the effective transformation and transformed-input averaging.
Appendix A.3 distinguishes exact Haar projection from local averaging, which suppresses non-equivariant components.
contexts.proposed_replacement: Replace “This classical Reynolds-operator construction cancels architecture-specific, transform-dependent noise while preserving” with “This Reynolds-inspired averaging can suppress architecture-specific, transform-dependent artifacts while retaining”.

contexts.evidence: Appendix A.1.4 preserves centering; Appendix E does not claim completeness for biased ViTs.
contexts.proposed_replacement: The averaging pairs naturally with a conditioned forward pass inspired by DAVE~\parencite{Wrobel2024}. Our game implementation fixes both LayerNorm statistics, the GELU gate and the softmax row; DAVE instead retains linear mean-centering while fixing the normalization scale. Conservation here concerns the game’s conditioned propagation rule, including its bias accounting.

contexts.evidence: DAVE is correctly identified as a transformer attribution baseline; the reported comparative numbers are thesis results.
Sections 3.1–3.4 establish the described distribution-aware ViT gradient decomposition.

notes: The legacy key Wrobel2024 is retained, but this DAVE paper is from 2026, now published at ICML.

Main substantive correction: DAVE Appendix A.1.4 retains mean-centering as C=I−11ᵀ/d and freezes inverse standard deviation. Freezing both mean and standard deviation, as the thesis implements, is a different conditioned operator.
DAVE already freezes attention weights, so QK gradient detachment is not an addition to DAVE.

Appendix E explicitly distinguishes effective-transformation attribution from strict completeness for biased standard ViTs. Conservation of the thesis routing rule requires its own argument and bias accounting.

DAVE averages effective operators and multiplies the result by the original input (Algorithm 2), with additional noise. The thesis may adopt a different no-noise smoothing mode, but should call it an adaptation.
Official code saved as papers/Wrobel2024_detach_mode.py. No thesis experiments were reproduced in this reference audit.
